what: PANELS-WRITER (2026-10-18): BF16-PANELS-1's writers derive each 32-row block's second panel (B's pairs, or A^T's transposed words) from the A panel they have just written; the candidate measured here is a strip writer that never reads the A panel back -- 32 rows by a strip of columns of binary32 values held in L1, the A panel written a tile at a time, the second panel converted from the same binary32 values by the same conversion (so the same bits) -- at strips of 64, 128 and 256 columns, with and without streamed stores; and the shipped writer with its second panel, or both panels, streamed. Then the shipped writer's time split: its row segments' values alone (no panel), its A panels alone (no second panel), and the whole writer. All at the decoder's SwiGLU shape (1024 x 1024) on huge pages, each driver's arms rotated round by round in one process, every candidate's panels compared with the shipped writer's byte for byte at the end of every round.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207: AMX-BF16 and AVX512-BF16; the instance of ../), GCC 13.3, -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno (the library's build options), Python 3.11.15; head 992e333 (runtime/c identical to 5804ad5's); indicative wall times, no PMU
reading: The strip writer is slower than the shipped writer at every strip width and store kind, at both thread counts (screen-t4.txt: x0.751-0.977 for the SiLU product, x0.674-0.970 for the VJP; screen-t1.txt: x0.604-0.990 and x0.546-0.894), its panels identical. Streaming the shipped writer's second panel reads x0.978 and x1.061 at four threads and x0.985 and x0.987 at one, both panels streamed x0.840-0.965; in the step the GEMMs that read the panels follow soon after (the VJP's A^T panels by the weight adjoints in the same job), where streamed stores would send them past the caches. Nothing here is kept. The split (split-t4.txt, split-t1.txt) says what the writer's second panel costs: at four threads the values alone are 82% (SiLU) and 62% (VJP) of the shipped writer's time and its A panels alone 83% and 69% -- the second panels 17% and 31% -- the binary32 entries 76% and 60%; at one thread the second panels are 12% and 22%. The second panel's cost is its interleave and transpose, bit moves on the shuffle port, not the read of the A panel the strip writer avoids, and converting twice in short strips costs more than reading back from L1.

files.run.sh: the records in order (bash run.sh OUT from the repository root): the strip writer and the store kinds patched into a copy of runtime/c/bcir_tensor.c, the split flags into that copy, both drivers built with the library's options, four threads then one
files.patch_v4.py: the strip writer (bcir_tensor_*_panels4_pool) and the shipped writer with streamed stores (bcir_tensor_*_panels_nt_pool), inserted into a copy
files.split.py: the timing-only flags on the shipped writer of that copy: the values without panels, the A panels without the second
files.pw.c, screen-t4.txt, screen-t1.txt: the candidates against the shipped writer and the binary32 entries, medians of 41 rounds at four threads and 21 at one, each candidate's ratio to the shipped writer and its byte comparison
files.pw_split.c, split-t4.txt, split-t1.txt: the shipped writer's time split, each part as a share of the whole writer's time
